On 17 March 2026, the CAF Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match for temporarily refusing to play and leaving the pitch in protest of a refereeing decision.<ref name="BBC">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/ce949glzzglo |title=Morocco awarded Afcon title after CAF overturns result |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=17 March 2026 |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref> Pursuant to articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, the final was awarded as a 3–0 win for Morocco, thereby retroactively declaring them as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions and stripping Senegal of the title.<ref name="appeal">{{cite web |url=https://www.cafonline.com/news/caf-appeal-board-media-statement/ |title=CAF Appeal Board Media Statement |publisher=Confederation of African Football|date=17 March 2026 |access-date=17 March 2026|archive-date=17 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317220033/http://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://www.cafonline.com/news/caf-appeal-board-media-statement/ |url-status=live }}</ref>}}
| most successful team = {{nowrap|{{fb|EGY}} (7 titles)}}
}}
The [[Africa Cup of Nations]] is a football competition established in 1957. It is contested by the men's national teams of members of the [[Confederation of African Football]] (CAF), the African governing body for the sport, and is held every two years. The winner of the first final was [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]], who defeated [[Ethiopia national football team|Ethiopia]] 4–0 in [[Khartoum]] after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]].<ref>{{cite web |title=African Nations Cup 1957 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tables/57a.html |access-date=6 September 2017 |publisher=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> The [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations final|most recent final]] was played in [[Rabat]] in January 2026; [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] won the match by forfeiture after [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]]'s national team had decided to abandon the match during regular time.<ref name="BBC"/><ref name="appeal"/>

The Africa Cup of Nations final is the last match of the competition, and the result determines which team declared African champions. As of the 2025 edition, if the score is tied after 90 minutes of regular play, an additional 30-minute period of play, called [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]], is added. If such a match remains tied after extra time, it is decided by a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. The team that wins the penalty shoot-out is then declared the champions.

The 34 finals{{refn|name=1959final|group=n}} to-date have produced thirteen drawn matches, the eventual winners of which have been determined variously by [[Replay (sports)|replay]] ([[1974 African Cup of Nations final|1974]]), extra time ([[1962 African Cup of Nations final|1962]], [[1962 African Cup of Nations final|1965]], [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations final|2025]]), or penalty shoot-out ([[1982 African Cup of Nations final|1982]], [[1986 African Cup of Nations final|1986]], [[1992 African Cup of Nations final|1992]], [[2000 Africa Cup of Nations final|2000]], [[2002 Africa Cup of Nations final|2002]], [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations final|2006]], [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations final|2012]], [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations final|2015]], [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations final|2021]]). [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] is the most successful team in the history of the tournament, winning seven times.

The tournament winner was decided by a final round-robin group contested by four teams (Morocco, Guinea, Nigeria, and Egypt). Coincidentally, one of the last two matches of the tournament pitted the two top ranked teams against each other, with [[Guinea v Morocco (1976 African Cup of Nations)|Morocco's 1–1 draw with Guinea]] thus often being considered the de facto final of the 1976 African Cup of Nations.
